issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap or rotation policy
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler appends every root-logger record into self.buffer with no maxlen, no size cap, no time bound. If session.start() takes minutes (slow connect, retry storms, hanging dependency import), the buffer grows monotonically. State the invariant in code: 'buffer holds at most N records or M bytes; oldest dropped on overflow.' A bounded deque(maxlen=...) is the right data structure here.

issues.description: O(H) handler scan on every shutdown and every replay with no invariant stated
issues.detail: Both _shutdown_telemetry and _flush_early_log_buffer iterate logging.getLogger().handlers searching for LoggingHandler instances. The replay path breaks after the first match, silently assuming exactly one OTLP handler; the shutdown path removes all matches. These two functions disagree on the invariant. State it once ('exactly one OTLP LoggingHandler is attached after _setup_cloud_tracer') and assert it, or hold a direct reference.

issues.description: Replay path silently drops buffered records when no OTLP handler is found
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer iterates handlers looking for a LoggingHandler; if _setup_cloud_tracer failed or attached under a different name, the for-loop completes without the break and the buffered records are discarded with no warning. The whole point of this PR is not losing crash logs. Log a warning, or assert the handler exists; do not fail silently.

issues.description: _on_cleanup re-enters init_recording on crash with no documented precondition
issues.detail: When the early handler is set and _recording_initialized is False, cleanup calls init_recording with audio=False, traces=False, logs=True. This implicitly assumes init_recording is safe to invoke from the cleanup path, that _setup_cloud_tracer is idempotent enough, and that the OTLP exporter can be brought up after a crash. None of this is stated. A literate comment naming the precondition and the failure mode is needed; right now the rationale lives only in the PR description.

issues.description: Parallel test execution removed from makefile with no stated reason
issues.detail: unit-tests drops '-n auto' and removes test_plugin_google_stt.py from the suite. No comment, no commit-message reference. If pytest-xdist exposed a real flake, document it; if it is a workaround for this PR's logging changes (handler state leaking across workers is plausible), say so. Otherwise this is a measurable CI-time regression with no audit trail.

issues.description: Buffered records replayed without re-checking level or filters
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.emit appends every record passed to it; the replay loop calls h.emit(record) directly, bypassing the OTLP handler's level filter and any attached filters. Records that the OTLP handler would normally drop will be exported on crash. State the intended semantics ('crash path exports everything regardless of level') or route through handle() instead of emit() so filters apply.

review.summary: The PR's intent is sound — buffer logs early, replay on crash — but the implementation is under-audited in the Knuth sense: no stated invariants on buffer size, no stated invariant on how many OTLP handlers exist, and silent failure modes where the buffered crash logs (the whole point) can be dropped without a warning. The handler-discovery pattern is duplicated in two places that disagree on whether one or many OTLP handlers may exist; hold a direct reference and assert the invariant instead. Smaller concerns: replay bypasses handler-level filtering, _on_cleanup re-entering init_recording deserves a literate comment naming its precondition, and the makefile change (removing -n auto and a test file) ships with no audit trail. None of these block correctness on the happy path, but the PR is fixing an observability gap — silent failures in the fix itself are the worst class of bug here.
